Diego / Laura / Hannah —

Technical notes from infra/security:

- Hosted EU endpoints: customer content (requests/responses) and request-level persistent logs are stored in EU region buckets for customers whose tenancy is configured in EU region. Short-lived debug traces used for live troubleshooting are ephemeral and scrubbed; by default we do not route request payloads outside EU for EU-hosted accounts.
- Control plane telemetry (aggregated metrics, health events) may be processed in the control plane which currently runs some services in the US. This telemetry does not contain customer content, but it may include metadata (request counts, error rates). For customers requiring strict EU-only processing of all telemetry, we offer Private deployment / control plane in-customer-VPC or our EU-only private tenancy option.
- Keys: we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) via EU KMS in Dedicated/Private. For hosted customers, we can enable EU KMS where available — for guarantees we recommend Dedicated with customer-managed KMS.
- Deletion evidence: we can run an automated export that contains object identifiers, deletion request time, and storage lifecycle completion markers. For backups, completion depends on backup retention windows; typical timeline: primary delete propagated within 24-72 hours, backups purged on their next rotation (configurable, often 30 days). We can supply hashes/timestamps as proof.

Attachments Im attaching: inregion-logging-checklist.xlsx with toggles to remove debug traces and limit retention, plus a proposed runbook for generating deletion evidence. If MediHealth wants, we can schedule a 45-minute technical workshop and demo of the evidence export process.

—Rishi

Thanks for the patience. Please find the consolidated answers and the documents attached:

1) EU-only processing: For customers configured on EU-hosted endpoints or Dedicated pools, customer content and persistent request logs are stored in EU data stores. Control-plane aggregated telemetry may be processed outside the EU unless you select Dedicated/Private that includes an EU control plane.

2) SCCs & contract: Attached is our standard SCCs addendum (sccs-template-2027.pdf). Laura has reviewed and marked it Legal Approved — please review and let us know any redlines. We can countersign once procurement/legal confirm.

3) KMS & keys: We support EU KMS and customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private. For strict key residency we recommend Dedicated with customer-managed KMS; for hosted customers we can enable EU KMS where available (well confirm region availability for your tenant).

4) Retention & deletion evidence: We can provide a deletion evidence package containing object IDs, deletion timestamps, and storage lifecycle completion markers. Primary data deletion is typically initiated immediately and completes within 24-72 hours; backups follow configured retention windows (default 30 days). We are including a one-pager that describes the export fields and timeline.

5) Subprocessors: current subprocessors list is included in the share (link above) and in the SCCs addendum. If any non-EEA subprocessor has access to customer content, we will document mitigation controls as part of the DPA.

Next steps:
- Please review attached: redwood-eu-arch-v1.pdf, sccs-template-2027.pdf, inregion-logging-checklist.xlsx, and the deletion-evidence-onepager.pdf (attached inline).
- If acceptable, Hannah will coordinate a 45-minute technical workshop with Rishi and our infra team. Proposed slots: Tue 16th (09:00-09:45 CET) or Thu 18th (15:00-15:45 CET). We are happy to accommodate other times as needed.
